LESSON: WRITING 3.5.1 STRUCTURE OF A PARAGRAPH

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.5: Writing 3.5.1 Structure of a paragraph

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 3.5.1 Structure of a paragraph. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important to organise ideas in your paragraphs coherently?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. create a paragraph that is well developed, coherent and unified

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 3.5.1 STRUCTURE OF A PARAGRAPH
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 3.5.1 Structure of a paragraph helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 3.5.1 STRUCTURE OF A PARAGRAPH
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Create a paragraph that is well developed, coherent and unified

What this means
In this part you learn to create a paragraph that is well developed, coherent and unified. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create a paragraph that is well developed, coherent and unified.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 3.5.1 Structure of a paragraph”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create a paragraph that is well developed, coherent and unified. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 3.5.1 Structure of a paragraph is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 3.5.1 Structure of a paragraph”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: create a paragraph that is well developed, coherent and unified)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 3.5.1 Structure of a paragraph to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: create a paragraph that is well developed, coherent and unified.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 3.5.1 Structure of a paragraph from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 3.5.1 Structure of a paragraph: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Writing 3.5.1 Structure of a paragraph?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to organise ideas in your paragraphs coherently?
2. How can you ensure that your paragraphs are well formed?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 3.5.1 Structure of a paragraph means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: create a paragraph that is well developed, coherent and unified.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
